questions.prompt: Which access modifier makes a member accessible only within the same class?
questions.explanation: The 'private' modifier restricts access to the containing class only. Members declared private cannot be accessed from outside the class, even from derived classes.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: Which access modifier allows a member to be accessed from anywhere, including derived classes and other assemblies?
questions.template: The _____ modifier allows access from anywhere.

questions.prompt: Arrange these access modifiers from most permissive to least permissive (for members of a class):
A derived class accesses inherited fields on itself, and external code accesses fields through an instance. Which set of lines compiles?
questions.explanation: The derived class can access public, protected, and same-assembly internal fields (lines 1, 3, and 4). External code can access only the public field (line 5).

questions.prompt: What does the 'internal' access modifier do?
options: Accessible only within the same class
Accessible within the same assembly and any derived classes in that assembly
questions.explanation: 'Internal' members are accessible from anywhere within the same assembly. If combined with 'protected' (protected internal), they are also accessible from derived classes in other assemblies.

questions.prompt: Complete the member declaration to make it accessible only within the same assembly.
Which of the following is true about 'protected internal'?
options: Accessible only from the same class
Accessible from within the same assembly OR from derived classes (even in other assemblies)
questions.explanation: 'protected internal' is a combination: it is accessible from within the same assembly, or from a derived class regardless of which assembly the derived class is in. It is a logical OR, not AND.

questions.prompt: Which keyword restricts a member to be accessible only from derived classes?
Match each access modifier pair to its meaning. Order by: most restrictive, then broader.
items: private protected - accessible within the same assembly and only from derived classes within that assembly
private - accessible only within the containing class
protected internal - same assembly or derived classes

questions.prompt: Which field can unrelated code in a different assembly access through an instance of MyClass?
options: The public field A and internal field D
The public field A and protected field C
questions.explanation: Unrelated code in another assembly can access only public members. Private, protected, and internal fields are not accessible there.
